events.title: World: Crop Prospects and Food Situation Triannual Global Report No. 3, November 2026
events.summary: Country: World Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Please refer to the attached file. Synopsis (short abstract) The triannual Crop Prospects and Food Situation report provides a forward-looking global analysis of cereal production, market trends and acute food security conditions, with a particular attention on low-income food-deficit countries. FAO estimates that 41 countries/territories require external assistance for food: 31 in Africa, eight in Asia, one in Latin America and the Caribbean, and one in Europe. Persisting conflicts and insecurity remain the primary drivers of the most severe levels of acute food insecurity, while weather shocks associated with the strong El Niño event are worsening conditions in several subregions. Looking ahead, El Niño-related impacts on production are expected to remain severe into 2027 in several subregions, likely aggravating acute food insecurity further. The report also includes FAO's latest forecast for 2026 cereal production among the Low-Income Food-Deficit Countries (LIFDCs), pegged at 126.5 million tonnes, about 2 percent above both the 2025 level and the five-year average. The increase largely reflects a strong production recovery in Asia, particularly in Near East Asia, while production among African LIFDCs is expected to remain near-average.

events.summary: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. Community engagement and communication : UNICEF-supported household visits reached over 1.2 million people, while dialogues engaged a further 30,000 people and 1,390 gatekeepers and influencers. OCV : 701,354 vaccinations supported in Lusaka, Chibombo and Chongwe (23–26 October 2026). WASH : UNICEF delivered 20 AWD kits to five districts and two tents to Chibombo for cholera treatment centres. It supported three inline chlorinators in Chibombo and WASH/IPC supplies to 20 health facilities in Chibombo and to treatment facilities in four Luapula districts. Funding : UNICEF’s cholera response 2026/27 is only 9% funded, with a US$2.95 million gap (91%); Health has the largest gap (US$1.64 million). events.summary: Country: Pakistan Sources: International Organization for Migration, UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs Please refer to the attached file. 1. General Pakistan experiences winter conditions primarily from November to February, with severe cold and snowfall concentrated in northern and high-altitude regions. Winter-related hazards include cold waves, heavy snowfall, avalanches, landslides, blizzards and fog, with varying impacts across the country. Mountainous areas face extreme temperatures and seasonal isolation, while communities in the plains may experience cold nights and damp conditions. While Pakistan did not experience a major nationwide climate-related disaster in 2026 comparable to the previous year's floods, localized flooding affected parts of Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Balochistan, resulting in localized damage to housing, infrastructure and livelihoods. An earthquake in the Upper Hunza area near the Wakhan Corridor further heightened concerns for affected mountain communities, where prolonged winters, sub-zero temperatures and seasonal access restrictions can significantly increase exposure risks. Households with damaged or inadequate shelters, particularly those in remote high-altitude settlements, may face heightened vulnerabilities during winter 2026–27. These localized impacts, together with residual vulnerabilities from previous disasters, reinforce the need for geographically targeted gender and age-responsive winterization assistance based on verified household needs and current shelter conditions. The Platform will consolidate existing de-identified AAP data from a range of sources into a format that allows us to identify trends, identify emerging issues, and inform programmatic adjustments at the inter-agency level, and ensure that decisions from leadership are influenced by community data. events.title: Syrian Arab Republic: Population Mobility and Baseline Assessment — Round 20 (01–30 September 2026)
events.summary: Countries: Syrian Arab Republic, Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye Source: International Organization for Migration Please refer to the attached file. Since the transition of power on 8 December 2024, the Syrian Arab Republic (hereafter referred to as Syria) has experienced substantial shifts in its humanitarian, political, and demographic landscape. Population movements remain dynamic, with returns recorded across all 14 governorates alongside continued displacement. While changing security conditions have influenced mobility patterns, persistent gaps in housing, livelihoods, and access to essential services continue to affect the ability of returnees to re-establish their lives and sustain their return. The escalation of hostilities across the Middle East since 28 February 2026 has further influenced displacement dynamics, contributing to continued cross-border movements. This report presents mobility trends recorded during September 2026 by the International Organization Migration's (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), together with updated baseline estimates for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), IDP returnees within Syria, and arrivals from abroad, including both those returning to their areas of origin and those settling elsewhere. This report should be read alongside Communities of Return Index Round 5 for additional context. The findings in this report provide an evidence base to support humanitarian response, early recovery programming and planning for durable solutions.

events.title: Guatemala: Análisis de inseguridad alimentaria aguda de la CIF - Actualización de Análisis octubre 2026 - febrero 2027, Publicado el 19 de noviembre de 2026
events.summary: Country: Guatemala Source: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification Please refer to the attached file. Resumen El presente análisis de Inseguridad Alimentaria Aguda (IAA) corresponde a la actualización de la segunda situación proyectada para el período de octubre de 2026 a febrero de 2027. Esta actualización responde principalmente a la necesidad de incorporar los efectos de la intensificación del fenómeno de El Niño y de la sequía agrícola, que han afectado especialmente al Corredor Seco guatemalteco, provocando un deterioro de las condiciones de seguridad alimentaria, particularmente en 11 departamentos del país. Ante esta situación, el Gobierno de Guatemala declaró, el 11 de septiembre de 2026, una alerta naranja a nivel nacional por sequía (Anexo 1), con el propósito de fortalecer las medidas de preparación y respuesta frente a los efectos de la variabilidad climática. Durante julio y agosto de 2026, la marcada disminución de las precipitaciones prolongó el período de canícula y alteró los calendarios agrícolas, afectando principalmente los cultivos del ciclo de Primera. El déficit hídrico provocó pérdidas en la producción agrícola y contribuyó al agotamiento anticipado de las reservas de granos básicos de los hogares. Según el informe de afectaciones agropecuarias por fenómenos agroclimáticos y ambientales del Ministerio de Agricultura, Ganadería y Alimentación (MAGA), del 21 de septiembre de 2026, se registraron aproximadamente 252 801 hectáreas de cultivos afectadas y alrededor de 570 000 familias perjudicadas a nivel nacional. Paralelamente, el acceso económico a los alimentos se vio limitado por la reducción de las oportunidades de empleo e ingresos, especialmente entre los hogares que dependen de las actividades agrícolas y pecuarias en el Corredor Seco.
